questions.questionText: Neither of the two candidates ___ selected for the interview.
questions.explanation: 'Neither' is a singular pronoun, so it takes a singular verb: was.
questions.shortcut: Neither / Each / Either / One of + plural noun takes a singular verb.

questions.questionText: She has been working in this company ___ 2019.
questions.explanation: 'Since' is used with a fixed point in time (2019) with the present perfect continuous; 'for' is used with a period.
questions.shortcut: Point of time -> since; length of time -> for.

questions.questionText: Each of the students ___ given a certificate of merit.
questions.explanation: 'Each' is singular, so the verb is singular: was given.

questions.questionText: I am looking forward to ___ you at the wedding.
questions.explanation: In 'look forward to', 'to' is a preposition, so the verb that follows takes the -ing form.

questions.questionText: Of the two brothers, Ramesh is the ___.
questions.explanation: When two persons are compared, the comparative degree (taller) is used, not the superlative.
questions.shortcut: Two things -> comparative; three or more -> superlative.

questions.questionText: Hardly had he reached the platform ___ the train started moving.
questions.explanation: 'Hardly' (and 'scarcely') is followed by 'when'; 'than' goes with 'no sooner'.

questions.questionText: Unless you ___ hard, you will not pass the examination.
questions.explanation: 'Unless' already carries a negative meaning, so the verb that follows is affirmative, in the present tense for a future condition.

questions.questionText: The number of students in our college ___ increasing every year.
questions.explanation: 'The number of' takes a singular verb, because the subject is 'number'.
questions.shortcut: The number of -> singular; A number of -> plural.

questions.questionText: A number of students ___ absent from the class today.
questions.explanation: 'A number of' means 'several' and takes a plural verb.

questions.questionText: The books ___ I bought yesterday are very expensive.
questions.explanation: The relative pronoun for things is 'which'. 'What' cannot follow a noun, 'whom' is for persons and 'whose' shows possession.

questions.questionText: The man ___ car was stolen has lodged a complaint.
questions.explanation: The car belongs to the man, so the possessive relative pronoun 'whose' is required.

questions.questionText: The girl ___ I met at the airport is my cousin.
questions.explanation: 'Whom' is the object form for a person (I met her); 'whose', 'which' and 'what' do not fit.

questions.questionText: Of the two plans, this one is ___.
questions.explanation: Comparison of two items uses the comparative with 'the': the better.

questions.questionText: Gulliver's Travels ___ written by Jonathan Swift.
questions.explanation: A title of a book is treated as singular, and the sentence is about a past writing: was.
questions.shortcut: Book / film titles take singular verbs.

questions.questionText: Ten kilometres ___ a long distance to walk every day.
questions.explanation: A distance treated as a single unit takes a singular verb.

questions.questionText: If I ___ you, I would accept the offer immediately.
questions.explanation: For an unreal (imaginary) condition in the present, the subjunctive 'were' is used for all persons in standard grammar.

questions.questionText: The news of the victory ___ received with great joy.
questions.explanation: 'News' is an uncountable noun and takes a singular verb.
questions.shortcut: News, furniture, information, advice: always singular.

questions.questionText: By the time we reached the station, the train ___.
questions.explanation: Two past actions: the earlier one (the train leaving) is in the past perfect, the later (our reaching) in the simple past.
questions.shortcut: 'By the time' + simple past -> past perfect in main clause.

questions.questionText: One of my friends ___ a pilot in the Indian Air Force.
questions.explanation: 'One of + plural noun' takes a singular verb because the subject is 'One'.

questions.questionText: The teacher, along with her students, ___ going on a trip to Mysuru.
questions.explanation: 'Along with' does not make the subject plural; the verb agrees with 'The teacher', so it is singular.
questions.shortcut: Along with / together with / as well as: ignore the added noun.

questions.questionText: No sooner did he enter the hall ___ the lights went out.
questions.explanation: 'No sooner' is correctly followed by 'than'.

questions.questionText: Mathematics ___ my favourite subject since childhood.
questions.explanation: Names of subjects ending in -s (mathematics, physics, economics) are singular; 'since' needs the present perfect: has been.

questions.questionText: The scissors on the table ___ very sharp.
questions.explanation: 'Scissors' is a plural-only noun, so the verb is plural: are.

questions.questionText: I wish I ___ taller so that I could join the police force.
questions.explanation: After 'wish' referring to an unreal present situation, the subjunctive 'were' is used.

questions.questionText: Let us start the work now, ___?
questions.explanation: The question tag for 'Let us ...' is 'shall we'.

questions.questionText: He speaks as if he ___ the owner of the company.
questions.explanation: 'As if' expressing an unreal comparison takes the subjunctive 'were'.

questions.questionText: The more you practise, ___ you become.
questions.explanation: The structure 'the + comparative ..., the + comparative' needs 'the better'.

questions.questionText: Many a student ___ failed in this examination.
questions.explanation: 'Many a' is followed by a singular noun and a singular verb: has failed.
questions.shortcut: Many a + singular noun + singular verb.

questions.questionText: Either Meena or her cousins ___ coming to the party tonight.
questions.explanation: With 'either ... or', the verb agrees with the nearer subject, 'cousins' (plural): are.
questions.shortcut: Either/Neither ... or/nor: verb agrees with the nearest noun.

questions.questionText: Neither the manager nor his assistants ___ present at the meeting.
questions.explanation: With 'neither ... nor', the verb agrees with the nearer subject, 'assistants', so it is plural: were.

questions.questionText: I have never seen ___ elephant as tall as that one.
questions.explanation: 'Elephant' begins with a vowel sound, so the article 'an' is used.

questions.questionText: He bought ___ one-rupee coin from the shop.
questions.explanation: 'One' begins with the consonant sound /w/, so the article is 'a', not 'an'.
questions.shortcut: Article depends on sound, not spelling: a one-rupee, a university, an hour.

questions.questionText: If it rains tomorrow, we ___ the picnic.
questions.explanation: A real future condition (present tense in the if-clause) takes 'will' + base verb in the main clause.

questions.questionText: If she had studied harder, she ___ the examination.
questions.explanation: An unreal past condition (had studied) takes 'would have + past participle' in the main clause.
questions.shortcut: If + had + V3, ... would have + V3.

questions.questionText: She said that she ___ the film the previous day.
questions.explanation: In reported speech, a past action that came before the reporting verb is expressed in the past perfect: had seen.
questions.shortcut: Reported speech: simple past -> past perfect.

questions.questionText: The furniture in the old house ___ been sold.
questions.explanation: 'Furniture' is uncountable and singular, so 'has been' is correct.

questions.questionText: Ravi, as well as his friends, ___ invited to the function.
questions.explanation: 'As well as' does not change the number of the subject; 'Ravi' is singular, so the verb is singular.

questions.questionText: The patient ___ before the doctor arrived at the hospital.
questions.explanation: Two past events: the death happened before the doctor's arrival, so the earlier one takes the past perfect.

questions.questionText: The Principal, as well as the teachers, ___ attending the seminar tomorrow.
questions.explanation: 'As well as' does not make the subject plural; the subject is 'The Principal' (singular).

questions.questionText: He suggested that she ___ a doctor immediately.
questions.explanation: After verbs like suggest, insist, recommend and demand, a 'that' clause takes the base form of the verb (subjunctive): see.

questions.questionText: It is high time we ___ the problem seriously.
questions.explanation: 'It is high time' is followed by the simple past (past subjunctive) to show that action is overdue.

questions.questionText: He cannot swim across the river, ___?
questions.explanation: A negative statement takes a positive tag with the same auxiliary: cannot -> can he.

questions.questionText: She ___ her homework when the teacher entered the room.
questions.explanation: A past continuous action is interrupted by a simple past action (entered): was doing.

questions.questionText: The doctor suggested ___ to the hills for a few weeks.
questions.explanation: The verb 'suggest' is followed by a gerund (-ing form), not by an infinitive.

questions.questionText: He is used to ___ up early in the morning.
questions.explanation: In 'be used to', 'to' is a preposition, so the -ing form follows.

questions.questionText: I ___ in this city since I was a child.
questions.explanation: 'Since' with a point in the past and an action continuing to now needs the present perfect: have lived.

questions.questionText: Water ___ at 100 degrees Celsius at sea level.
questions.explanation: A scientific fact is expressed in the simple present; 'water' is singular, so boils.

questions.questionText: The doctor advised him to ___ from oily food for a few weeks.
questions.explanation: 'Abstain from' means to keep away from something; the other verbs do not take 'from' in this sense.

questions.questionText: Heavy rain ___ the match, so it was postponed to Sunday.
questions.explanation: The match was postponed, so the rain interrupted it: 'disrupted' fits.

questions.questionText: Ravi is very ___; he never tells a lie.
questions.explanation: Never telling a lie describes an honest person.

questions.questionText: The old man is so ___ that he donates half his pension to charity.
questions.explanation: Giving away money freely shows generosity; 'stingy' is the opposite.

questions.questionText: The sun was so ___ at noon that we could not walk barefoot on the road.
questions.explanation: Hot road surface needs an intensely hot sun: 'scorching'.

questions.questionText: The teacher praised Anita for her ___ in solving the toughest problem.
questions.explanation: Praise goes with a positive quality; 'ingenuity' means cleverness.

questions.questionText: The thief ___ the policeman by hiding behind a pillar.
questions.explanation: 'Elude' means to escape or avoid someone cleverly.

questions.questionText: He was so ___ after the long trek that he fell asleep immediately.
questions.explanation: Falling asleep at once follows extreme tiredness: 'exhausted'.

questions.questionText: Wearing a seat belt is ___ for the driver, as the law requires it.
questions.explanation: 'As the law requires it' means compulsory: 'mandatory'.

questions.questionText: The judge ___ the accused of all charges due to lack of evidence.
questions.explanation: Lack of evidence leads to being cleared of charges: 'acquitted'.

questions.questionText: The magician's trick left the audience ___; nobody could explain it.
questions.explanation: Being unable to explain something leaves people puzzled: 'baffled'.

questions.questionText: Rahul's ___ for cricket began when he received his first bat at the age of six.
questions.explanation: A gift that starts an interest in cricket creates a passion, not an aversion.

questions.questionText: The ___ of the old fort is a major tourist attraction in Rajasthan.
questions.explanation: Only 'grandeur' (magnificence) can attract tourists to a fort.

questions.questionText: The minister's speech was full of ___ promises that no one believed, as they were never kept.
questions.explanation: Promises never kept are 'empty' promises.

questions.questionText: Always arriving late and missing deadlines, he showed a ___ attitude towards his job.
questions.explanation: Lateness and missed deadlines show carelessness: 'negligent'.

questions.questionText: The scientist's theory was ___ by experiments conducted by two independent labs, confirming it.
questions.explanation: 'Confirming it' signals support: 'corroborated' means confirmed.

questions.questionText: The company's profits ___ sharply during the recession, forcing it to cut jobs.
questions.explanation: Job cuts follow a steep fall, so 'plummeted' fits.

questions.questionText: Being a ___ person, he never spends a rupee without thinking twice.
questions.explanation: Thinking twice before spending describes a thrifty (frugal) person.

questions.questionText: The two neighbours finally ___ their long-standing quarrel and became friends.
questions.explanation: Becoming friends means the quarrel was settled: 'resolved'.

questions.questionText: The lawyer gave a ___ argument that left no room for doubt.
questions.explanation: An argument leaving no doubt is convincing: 'cogent'.

questions.questionText: The crowd became ___ when the match was stopped unfairly and began throwing bottles.
questions.explanation: Throwing bottles shows disorderly behaviour: 'unruly'.

questions.questionText: Her ___ in the kitchen was evident from the perfect meal she cooked.
questions.explanation: A perfect meal shows skill: 'proficiency'.

questions.questionText: The patient's condition is ___; the doctors say he may not survive the night.
questions.explanation: Possible death overnight means a grave condition: 'critical'.

questions.questionText: The old professor was known for his ___ of speech; he could say a lot in a few words.
questions.explanation: Saying much in few words is 'brevity'; 'verbosity' is the opposite.

questions.questionText: The shopkeeper's ___ reply upset the customer, who had asked politely.
questions.explanation: A rude, abrupt reply to a polite question upsets: 'curt'.

questions.questionText: A good leader must be ___ and take quick decisions in a crisis.
questions.explanation: Quick decisions require being 'decisive'.

questions.questionText: The fire was ___ before it could spread to the neighbouring houses.
questions.explanation: Stopping it from spreading means it was put out: 'extinguished'.

questions.questionText: The students were ___ by the teacher for talking during the exam.
questions.explanation: Talking during an exam draws a scolding: 'reprimanded'.

questions.questionText: The explorers faced ___ weather on the peak, with blizzards and freezing winds.
questions.explanation: Blizzards and freezing winds are harsh: 'hostile'.

questions.questionText: Though wealthy, she led a ___ life, avoiding show and luxury.
questions.explanation: 'Avoiding show and luxury' describes a modest life.

questions.questionText: The two parties could not reach a ___ and the talks collapsed.
questions.explanation: One 'reaches a compromise' in negotiations; the other nouns do not collocate with 'reach' here.

questions.questionText: The new software is ___ with all the older versions, so files open without trouble.
questions.explanation: 'Compatible with' means able to work together.

questions.questionText: The CEO's sudden ___ shocked the board, as he had held the post for only a month.
questions.explanation: Leaving a post after a month is a resignation.

questions.questionText: The soldiers showed great ___ in the face of enemy fire.
questions.explanation: Courage under fire is 'valour'.

questions.questionText: The politician's ___ remarks about the minority community sparked widespread protests.
questions.explanation: Protests follow insulting remarks: 'derogatory' means disparaging.

questions.questionText: The report was so ___ that it covered every minor detail of the project.
questions.explanation: Covering every minor detail means thorough: 'exhaustive'.

questions.questionText: Hari's ___ nature made him adjust easily to any new city he was posted to.
questions.explanation: Adjusting easily shows adaptability.

questions.questionText: The judge's verdict was ___, favouring neither side.
questions.explanation: 'Favouring neither side' = impartial; 'partial' means biased.

questions.questionText: Despite repeated warnings, he continued his ___ driving and finally met with an accident.
questions.explanation: Ignoring warnings and crashing shows reckless driving.

questions.questionText: The minister's ___ response to the question avoided giving a direct answer.
questions.explanation: Avoiding a direct answer is 'evasive'.

questions.questionText: The doctor's ___ treatment of a minor ailment was criticised as an overreaction.
questions.explanation: Overreaction implies extreme measures: 'drastic'.

questions.questionText: Her speech was so ___ that half the audience began to yawn.
questions.explanation: Yawning shows boredom caused by a dull, unvarying speech: 'monotonous'.

questions.questionText: The soup was so ___ that the child refused to ___ it.
questions.explanation: A child refuses food that tastes bitter; 'swallow' completes the idea.

questions.questionText: The students were ___ when the teacher announced that the test was ___.
questions.explanation: Cancellation of a test pleases students; the other pairs are illogical.

questions.questionText: ___ it was raining heavily, the match ___ on time.
questions.explanation: Contrast between rain and starting on time needs 'Although'.

questions.questionText: The more you practise, the ___ you become and the ___ mistakes you make.
questions.explanation: Comparative 'better'; 'fewer' with countable 'mistakes'.

questions.questionText: She topped the class because she is ___ intelligent ___ hardworking.
questions.explanation: Topping the class needs positive qualities joined by 'both ... and'.

questions.questionText: ___ Ravi ___ his brother has passed the exam; both failed.
questions.explanation: 'Both failed' means neither passed: 'Neither ... nor'.

questions.questionText: By the time I ___ home, the match ___ already begun.
questions.explanation: Past event with an earlier past action takes simple past + past perfect (had begun).

questions.questionText: If he ___ harder, he ___ the exam.
questions.explanation: Third conditional: if + past perfect, would have + past participle.

questions.questionText: The ___ of the hotel's food was so ___ that guests kept returning.
questions.explanation: Guests return when food quality is excellent.

questions.questionText: She is taller ___ her sister but not as fair ___ her.
questions.explanation: Comparative 'taller' takes 'than'; 'not as fair' takes 'as'.

questions.questionText: Please ___ me your pen; I will ___ it back tomorrow.
questions.explanation: You lend something to someone; the borrower returns it.

questions.questionText: The ___ of the movie was so ___ that people left halfway.
questions.explanation: People leave a movie when the plot is dull.

questions.questionText: The patient was ___ to hospital after he ___ unconscious.
questions.explanation: Past passive 'was rushed' and past 'fell' (sequence of past events).

questions.questionText: Not only ___ he win the race, ___ he broke the record.
questions.explanation: 'Not only did he ..., but ...' is the correct inversion pattern.

questions.questionText: Unless you ___ hard, you will ___ the exam.
questions.explanation: 'Unless' already carries a negative; the result of not working is failing.

questions.questionText: The accused was ___ because the evidence was too ___ to convict him.
questions.explanation: Weak evidence cannot convict, so he was acquitted.

questions.questionText: Of the two candidates Arun is the ___ qualified, but among all the staff Meera is the ___ qualified.
questions.explanation: Two items: comparative 'more'; many items: superlative 'most'.

questions.questionText: He ___ to the doctor, but the doctor ___ already left.
questions.explanation: Earlier past action (left) takes past perfect 'had'.

questions.questionText: Because the road was ___, the bus ___ slowly.
questions.explanation: Adjective 'slippery' describes the road; past tense 'moved'.

questions.questionText: The harder she studies, the ___ marks she ___.
questions.explanation: 'The + comparative' pattern; singular subject takes 'scores'.

questions.questionText: My uncle, ___ lives in Pune, ___ a retired engineer.
questions.explanation: 'Who' is the subject for a person; singular subject takes 'is'.

questions.questionText: The book ___ I bought yesterday ___ very interesting.
questions.explanation: 'Which' for things; 'book' is singular so 'is'.

questions.questionText: He ___ for the bus for an hour when it finally ___.
questions.explanation: Past perfect continuous for the earlier ongoing action; simple past for the later event.

questions.questionText: The river ___ its banks and ___ the villages.
questions.explanation: Past of overflow is 'overflowed'; the water 'flooded' the villages.

questions.questionText: Neither the captain ___ the players ___ ready for the final.
questions.explanation: 'Neither' pairs with 'nor'; the verb agrees with the nearer subject, 'players' (were).

questions.questionText: A number of students ___ absent, but the number of absentees ___ small.
questions.explanation: 'A number of' takes plural; 'the number of' takes singular.

questions.questionText: I would have called you if I ___ your number, but I ___ it.
questions.explanation: Third conditional needs 'had known'; the real fact is past: 'did not know'.

questions.questionText: He is ___ MBA and his brother is ___ engineer.
questions.explanation: Article depends on sound: 'MBA' begins with the vowel sound 'em', and 'engineer' with a vowel.

questions.questionText: She is senior ___ me ___ three years.
questions.explanation: 'Senior' takes 'to'; the difference is shown with 'by'.

questions.questionText: He prefers tea ___ coffee, ___ his sister prefers coffee to tea.
questions.explanation: 'Prefer' takes 'to'; the two preferences contrast, so 'but'.

questions.questionText: She has ___ been to Goa, so she is ___ excited about the trip.
questions.explanation: 'Never' fits the 'so' clause of excitement; 'ever' is not used in a positive statement; 'very' goes with adjectives.

questions.questionText: Hardly ___ he sat down ___ the phone rang.
questions.explanation: 'Hardly had ... when' is the fixed pattern ('than' goes with 'no sooner').

questions.questionText: She ___ me yesterday that she ___ come the next day.
questions.explanation: 'Told' takes an object; the reported past needs 'would'.

questions.questionText: The principal, as well as the teachers, ___ pleased, and the students ___ also happy.
questions.explanation: 'As well as' does not change the subject (principal: was); 'students' takes 'were'.

questions.questionText: Had I ___ about the strike, I ___ left home earlier.
questions.explanation: Inverted third conditional: 'Had + past participle ..., would have + past participle'.

questions.questionText: Of the two proposals, the second is the ___ and it is also ___ practical.
questions.explanation: Two items need comparatives: better, more.

questions.questionText: She speaks as if she ___ the manager, though she ___ only a clerk.
questions.explanation: 'As if' for an unreal comparison takes 'were'; the fact is stated in present 'is'.

questions.questionText: The scheme, ___ aims at rural employment, ___ launched in 2006.
questions.explanation: 'Which' refers to the scheme (thing); singular 'was'.

questions.questionText: The flowers ___ I received were so ___ that the entire room smelt wonderful.
questions.explanation: 'Which' for things; smelling wonderful requires the adjective 'fragrant'.

questions.questionText: Seldom ___ he lose his temper, and rarely ___ he complain.
questions.explanation: Negative adverbs at the start take auxiliary inversion; singular 'he' takes 'does'.

questions.questionText: Each of the boys ___ his own bag, and all of them ___ ready to leave.
questions.explanation: 'Each' is singular (has); 'all of them' is plural (are).

questions.questionText: Rohan is not ___ clever ___ his sister, but he works harder.
questions.explanation: Negative equality uses 'as ... as'; 'than' never follows 'as'.

questions.questionText: The train arrives ___ platform number 4.
questions.explanation: A specific point or location such as a platform takes 'at'.

questions.questionText: She was born ___ 12 March 1998.
questions.explanation: Dates and days take 'on'.
questions.shortcut: Date/day -> on; month/year -> in; clock time -> at.

questions.questionText: The meeting will begin ___ 10 a.m. sharp.
questions.explanation: Exact clock times take 'at'.

questions.questionText: My brother is very good ___ mathematics.
questions.explanation: The adjective 'good' takes 'at' when it refers to a skill.

questions.questionText: The shopkeeper divided the sweets ___ the four children equally.
questions.explanation: 'Among' is used for more than two persons or things.
questions.shortcut: Two -> between; three or more -> among.

questions.questionText: There is a strong friendship ___ Ravi and Karthik.
questions.explanation: 'Between' is used for two persons.

questions.questionText: He has been absent ___ Monday.
questions.explanation: 'Since' marks a starting point in time.

questions.questionText: The students have been preparing ___ three months.
questions.explanation: 'For' is used with a period of time.

questions.questionText: The cat jumped ___ the wall and ran away.
questions.explanation: Passing above and across an obstacle is expressed by 'over'.

questions.questionText: He is married ___ a doctor from Madurai.
questions.explanation: The verb 'married' (state) is followed by 'to'.

questions.questionText: I am fond ___ filter coffee.
questions.explanation: The adjective 'fond' takes 'of'.

questions.questionText: She is afraid ___ lizards.
questions.explanation: The adjective 'afraid' is always followed by 'of' (afraid of lizards). 'From', 'at' and 'by' do not collocate with it.

questions.questionText: The farmers were happy ___ the heavy rain.
questions.explanation: 'Happy about' a situation or news is the standard usage here.

questions.questionText: He is accused ___ stealing the bicycle.
questions.explanation: 'Accuse' is followed by 'of'.

questions.questionText: The minister congratulated the team ___ their victory.
questions.explanation: 'Congratulate' takes 'on'.

questions.questionText: She insisted ___ paying the bill herself.
questions.explanation: The verb 'insist' takes the preposition 'on' before a gerund: insist on paying. Other prepositions are not used with it.

questions.questionText: The old man is suffering ___ high blood pressure.
questions.explanation: 'Suffer' takes 'from' for an ailment.

questions.questionText: He prefers tea ___ coffee.
questions.explanation: 'Prefer' is followed by 'to', not 'than'.

questions.questionText: The bridge is ___ construction and will open next year.
questions.explanation: 'Under construction' is the fixed phrase.

questions.questionText: She is senior ___ me by two years.
questions.explanation: Adjectives like senior, junior, superior, inferior take 'to'.

questions.questionText: The Principal was angry ___ the students for their misbehaviour.
questions.explanation: Anger toward a person takes 'with' (at is used for a thing).
questions.shortcut: angry with a person; angry at a thing.

questions.questionText: The thief was caught ___ the act of breaking the lock.
questions.explanation: The idiom is 'caught in the act'.

questions.questionText: He is tired ___ waiting for the bus.
questions.explanation: 'Tired of' means fed up with doing something.

questions.questionText: The new law is applicable ___ all citizens.
questions.explanation: 'Applicable' is followed by 'to' (applicable to all citizens), never 'for' or 'on'.

questions.questionText: The company has been in business ___ 1985.
questions.explanation: A fixed starting year with the present perfect takes 'since'.

questions.questionText: I will finish this work ___ Friday at the latest.
questions.explanation: 'By' means not later than a deadline; 'till' would show continuous activity up to Friday.

questions.questionText: The shop remains open ___ 9 p.m. every day.
questions.explanation: 'Till' shows a situation continuing up to a time.

questions.questionText: The Himalayas lie ___ the north of India.
questions.explanation: A neighbouring region outside the boundary is described with 'to the north of'.
questions.shortcut: outside the area -> to the north of.

questions.questionText: Karnataka lies ___ the south of Maharashtra and is not part of it, so we say it lies ___ the south.
questions.explanation: Outside neighbours use 'to the south of'.

questions.questionText: She has no objection ___ your joining the team.
questions.explanation: The noun 'objection' takes 'to' (objection to your joining), even when a gerund follows. 'Against' is not used here.

questions.questionText: The teacher was pleased ___ the progress of her students.
questions.explanation: 'Pleased with' for a result or thing is standard; 'with' is used with progress.

questions.questionText: He died ___ cancer last year.
questions.explanation: 'Die of' is used with a disease (illness as cause).
questions.shortcut: die of disease; die from injury/overwork.

questions.questionText: The pilot was blamed ___ the accident.
questions.explanation: 'Blame somebody for something'.

questions.questionText: The Chief Guest was received ___ a bouquet.
questions.explanation: The instrument or manner of receiving is introduced by 'with'.

questions.questionText: She has a great aversion ___ crowded places.
questions.explanation: The noun 'aversion' is followed by 'to'.

questions.questionText: The jury differed ___ the verdict, so a retrial was ordered.
questions.explanation: 'Differ on' a matter (disagree about) is used here; 'differ from' compares things.
questions.shortcut: differ from = unlike; differ on/about = disagree.

questions.questionText: Her accent is quite different ___ her sister's.
questions.explanation: In standard Indian-English usage 'different' takes 'from'.

questions.questionText: The minister is the author ___ several bills on education.
questions.explanation: 'Author of' links a writer to the work: the author of several bills. 'By' would reverse the relationship.

questions.questionText: He was deprived ___ his inheritance by the court order.
questions.explanation: 'Deprive' is always followed by 'of': deprived of his inheritance. Similar patterns: robbed of, relieved of.

questions.questionText: The officer was entrusted ___ the responsibility of conducting the audit.
questions.explanation: Entrust somebody with something (or entrust something to somebody).

questions.questionText: The trustees are accountable ___ the shareholders for every rupee spent.
questions.explanation: Accountable to a person, for an action.

questions.questionText: The rebels were unwilling to comply ___ the ceasefire terms.
questions.explanation: 'Comply' takes 'with': comply with the terms. 'To' is used with 'conform' or 'adhere', not 'comply'.

questions.questionText: He decided to ___ up smoking for good.
questions.explanation: 'Give up' means to stop a habit. 'Bring up', 'hold up' and 'pull up' do not mean quitting.

questions.questionText: The flight will ___ off at 6 a.m.
questions.explanation: 'Take off' is the phrasal verb for an aircraft leaving the ground.

questions.questionText: Please ___ on the lights; it is getting dark.
questions.explanation: 'Turn on' means to switch on an appliance or light.

questions.questionText: I will ___ you up at the station at 5 p.m.
questions.explanation: 'Pick up' means to collect someone by vehicle. 'Fetch up' and 'drop up' are not used this way.

questions.questionText: Please jot ___ the new phone number in your diary.
questions.explanation: 'Jot down' means to write something briefly. The particle is 'down'.

questions.questionText: The thief tried to ___ away but was caught.
questions.explanation: 'Run away' means to flee. The other verbs do not combine with 'away' to give this meaning.

questions.questionText: If you do not know the meaning of a word, ___ it up in a dictionary.
questions.explanation: 'Look up' means to search for information in a reference book.

questions.questionText: Our car ___ down on the highway, so we reached late.
questions.explanation: 'Break down' means a machine stops working. 'Put down', 'set down' and 'take down' do not.

questions.questionText: Please ___ out the application form in capital letters.
questions.explanation: 'Fill out' means to complete a form by writing in the details.

questions.questionText: The machine will shut ___ automatically if it overheats.
questions.explanation: 'Shut down' means to stop operating; 'shut up', 'shut in' and 'shut by' have other meanings or are wrong here.

questions.questionText: He ___ up at 5 a.m. every day to go for a walk.
questions.explanation: 'Get up' means to rise from bed. 'Put up', 'go up' and 'take up' have different meanings.

questions.questionText: We have ___ out of sugar; please buy some on your way.
questions.explanation: 'Run out of' means to have no more of something left.
questions.shortcut: Run out of = finished the stock.

questions.questionText: The sisters ___ along very well and never quarrel.
questions.explanation: 'Get along' means to have a friendly relationship with someone.

questions.questionText: The police have promised to ___ into the robbery.
questions.explanation: 'Look into' means to investigate. The other verbs do not form a phrasal verb with 'into' in this sense.

questions.questionText: Don't ___ off the task till tomorrow; finish it today.
questions.explanation: 'Put off' means to postpone, which matches the idea of leaving it till tomorrow.

questions.questionText: He ___ across an old friend while shopping in Chennai.
questions.explanation: 'Come across' means to meet or find by chance.

questions.questionText: The firemen quickly ___ out the fire.
questions.explanation: 'Put out' means to extinguish a fire.

questions.questionText: The scheme fell ___ because of lack of funds.
questions.explanation: 'Fall through' means a plan fails to happen. 'Fell off', 'fell away' and 'fell behind' do not carry this sense.

questions.questionText: She takes ___ her mother in looks.
questions.explanation: 'Take after' means to resemble a parent or elder relative.

questions.questionText: The CEO will ___ down next March after twenty years.
questions.explanation: 'Step down' means to resign from a post.

questions.questionText: I cannot ___ up with his constant noise any longer.
questions.explanation: 'Put up with' means to tolerate, which suits 'cannot ... any longer'.

questions.questionText: The mechanic managed to ___ out what was wrong with the engine.
questions.explanation: 'Find out' means to discover a fact or reason.

questions.questionText: The manager asked him to ___ up the report by Friday.
questions.explanation: 'Draw up' means to prepare a formal document.

questions.questionText: He ___ up his mind to join the army.
questions.explanation: The fixed phrase is 'make up one's mind', meaning to decide.

questions.questionText: The teacher told the boys to ___ on with their work quietly.
questions.explanation: 'Get on with' means to continue doing something.

questions.questionText: The organisers had to ___ off the concert as the singer fell ill.
questions.explanation: 'Call off' means to cancel an event.

questions.questionText: After the war, the economy took years to ___ back.
questions.explanation: 'Bounce back' means to recover quickly after a setback.

questions.questionText: The students were asked to ___ in their assignments by Monday.
questions.explanation: 'Hand in' means to submit work.

questions.questionText: The old building was ___ down to build a mall.
questions.explanation: 'Pull down' means to demolish a building.

questions.questionText: He ___ out of the race due to an injury.
questions.explanation: 'Drop out' means to withdraw from a contest or course.

questions.questionText: She ___ up three children single-handedly.
questions.explanation: 'Bring up' means to raise a child.

questions.questionText: The bomb ___ off with a loud noise.
questions.explanation: 'Go off' means to explode. 'Come off', 'run off' and 'put off' do not.

questions.questionText: The negotiators ___ out a compromise after hours of talks.
questions.explanation: 'Work out' means to find a solution through effort.

questions.questionText: The meeting ___ on till midnight, leaving everyone exhausted.
questions.explanation: 'Drag on' means to continue for too long.

questions.questionText: The new manager has ___ up with a plan to cut costs.
questions.explanation: 'Come up with' means to think of an idea or plan.

questions.questionText: His speech ___ the audience up and they cheered for minutes.
questions.explanation: 'Fire up' means to fill with enthusiasm.

questions.questionText: She was ___ out by the tiring journey and slept at once.
questions.explanation: 'Worn out' means extremely tired.

questions.questionText: The doctor asked me to cut ___ on sweets.
questions.explanation: 'Cut back on' means to reduce consumption; 'cut off' would mean stop completely or sever, and is not followed by 'on'.

questions.questionText: The coach decided to ___ the new bowler out in the nets.
questions.explanation: 'Try out' means to test someone or something to judge ability.

questions.questionText: The old rivals finally ___ up and shook hands.
questions.explanation: 'Make up' means to become friends again after a quarrel.

questions.questionText: Nobody expected the plan to ___ out so well.
questions.explanation: 'Turn out' means to end up in a particular way.

questions.questionText: She has to ___ in for her sick colleague this week.
questions.explanation: 'Fill in for' means to substitute for someone temporarily.

questions.questionText: Rahul tried to ___ the crowd down but they kept shouting.
questions.explanation: 'Calm down' means to make or become less agitated.

questions.questionText: The teacher ___ over the lesson again before the exam.
questions.explanation: 'Go over' means to review or revise.

questions.questionText: The detective ___ the clues together and solved the case.
questions.explanation: 'Piece together' means to assemble information bit by bit.

questions.questionText: I think I ___ a mistake in the third answer.
questions.explanation: 'Make a mistake' is the fixed collocation; 'do a mistake' is wrong.

questions.questionText: Have you ___ your homework?
questions.explanation: 'Do homework' is the collocation; 'make homework' is incorrect.

questions.questionText: Please ___ attention to the instructions.
questions.explanation: The collocation is 'pay attention'.

questions.questionText: She ___ her promise and returned the money on time.
questions.explanation: 'Keep a promise' is the fixed collocation.

questions.questionText: We ___ a lot of fun at the picnic.
questions.explanation: 'Have fun' is the standard collocation.

questions.questionText: Can you ___ a photo of us?
questions.explanation: 'Take a photo' is the standard collocation.

questions.questionText: There was ___ rain last night, and the streets flooded.
questions.explanation: Rain is described as 'heavy', not 'strong' or 'big'.

questions.questionText: He ___ a lie to avoid punishment.
questions.explanation: 'Tell a lie' is the fixed collocation.
questions.shortcut: Tell a lie / a story; say a word.

questions.questionText: You must ___ care of your health during the exams.
questions.explanation: 'Take care of' is the fixed expression.

questions.questionText: Shall I ___ some tea for you?
questions.explanation: 'Make tea' is the collocation; 'cook tea' is not used.

questions.questionText: Take a taxi to ___ time.
questions.explanation: 'Save time' is the fixed collocation.

questions.questionText: Can you ___ a secret?
questions.explanation: 'Keep a secret' is the collocation.

questions.questionText: The baby was ___ asleep within minutes.
questions.explanation: 'Fast asleep' is a fixed collocation meaning deeply asleep.

questions.questionText: We must ___ an effort to reduce waste.
questions.explanation: 'Make an effort' is the fixed collocation.

questions.questionText: The government ___ a ban on plastic bags.
questions.explanation: 'Impose a ban' is the standard collocation.

questions.questionText: She drives a hard ___ with every supplier.
questions.explanation: 'Drive a hard bargain' is an idiom meaning to negotiate firmly.

questions.questionText: The minister ___ his resignation to the Prime Minister.
questions.explanation: 'Tender one's resignation' is the formal collocation.

questions.questionText: We should ___ a close watch on the situation.
questions.explanation: 'Keep a close watch' is the fixed collocation.

questions.questionText: The firm ___ heavy losses last year.
questions.explanation: Losses are 'incurred'; achieved, gained and won go with positive things.

questions.questionText: They ___ a warm welcome to the chief guest.
questions.explanation: 'Extend a welcome' is the formal collocation.

questions.questionText: It is time we ___ an end to this dispute.
questions.explanation: 'Put an end to' is the fixed expression.

questions.questionText: She ___ a deep sigh of relief.
questions.explanation: 'Heave a sigh' is the standard collocation.

questions.questionText: The detective ___ a blank when asked about the motive.
questions.explanation: 'Draw a blank' means to fail to find or recall anything.

questions.questionText: He was deep ___ debt after the business failed.
questions.explanation: 'Deep in debt' is the fixed collocation with 'in'.

questions.questionText: The passengers had a narrow ___ when the bus skidded.
questions.explanation: 'Narrow escape' is the fixed collocation.

questions.questionText: It is an open ___ that he plans to retire.
questions.explanation: 'Open secret' means something known to everyone though officially secret.

questions.questionText: The patient is in ___ condition after the accident.
questions.explanation: A seriously ill patient is in 'critical condition'.

questions.questionText: He ___ his best to reach on time.
questions.explanation: 'Do one's best' is the fixed collocation.

questions.questionText: The thief was caught ___-handed.
questions.explanation: 'Caught red-handed' is the idiom.

questions.questionText: She ___ a complaint with the police.
questions.explanation: 'Lodge a complaint' is the standard collocation.

questions.questionText: The company ___ bankrupt after the scam.
questions.explanation: 'Go bankrupt' is the fixed collocation.

questions.questionText: The jury ___ the wrong conclusion from the evidence.
questions.explanation: 'Draw a conclusion' is the standard collocation.

questions.questionText: The rule is hard and ___; no exceptions are allowed.
questions.explanation: 'Hard and fast rules' is a fixed phrase.

questions.questionText: She was ___ with grief after her father's death.
questions.explanation: 'Overcome with grief' is the standard collocation.

questions.questionText: The accused was granted ___ on a bond of ₹50,000.
questions.explanation: Release pending trial against a bond is 'bail'.

questions.questionText: The chief minister laid the ___ stone of the hospital.
questions.explanation: 'Lay the foundation stone' is the fixed expression.

questions.questionText: The villagers turned a ___ ear to the officer's appeal.
questions.explanation: 'Turn a deaf ear' means to refuse to listen.

questions.questionText: The candidate ___ his election promise within a year of winning.
questions.explanation: 'Break a promise' is the collocation.

questions.questionText: The neighbours finally buried the ___ and became friends.
questions.explanation: 'Bury the hatchet' is the idiom for ending a quarrel.

questions.questionText: Lack of sleep can ___ havoc with your health.
questions.explanation: 'Play havoc with' is the fixed expression.

questions.questionText: She has a sweet ___ and cannot resist desserts.
questions.explanation: 'Sweet tooth' means a liking for sweet food.

questions.questionText: The speaker was given a standing ___ at the end.
questions.explanation: 'Standing ovation' is the fixed collocation.

questions.questionText: The minister ___ the blame on the previous government.
questions.explanation: 'Lay the blame on' is the standard expression.

questions.questionText: The company ___ a profit of ₹5 crore this quarter.
questions.explanation: 'Make a profit' is the standard collocation.

questions.questionText: Do not take the matter ___; it is only a joke.
questions.explanation: 'Take lightly' is the standard collocation.

questions.questionText: He is a ___ sleeper and wakes at the slightest noise.
questions.explanation: 'Light sleeper' is the fixed collocation.

questions.questionText: Virat ___ the record for most centuries in the tournament.
questions.explanation: 'Break a record' is the collocation.

questions.questionText: Many small firms ___ business in this lane.
questions.explanation: 'Do business' is the collocation.

questions.questionText: Don't ___ your time on gossip.
questions.explanation: 'Waste time' is the collocation; 'pass time' means to occupy time and does not fit the warning.
